competitions.name: ASME Young Composers Awards (state-based)
competitions.pitch: A state-by-state comp for young composers, from solo instrument to rock, pop and EDM. Winning compositions are performed live at the awards ceremony.

competitions.name: Canberra Glassworks Kids' Design Competition
competitions.pitch: Draw a design on the theme Art in Bloom. Annette Blair blows the winning design in glass live at Floriade, and the finished piece goes home with the kid.
competitions.when: Entries close mid September, winning design blown in glass at Floriade in late September
competitions.where: Run in Canberra, no geographic limit stated, entries by post or email

competitions.name: National Water Week Poster Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by Victorian water corporations. Kids design a poster on the year's water theme, and category winners progress to state finals in National Water Week.

competitions.name: Book Links Short Story Writing Competition
competitions.pitch: A nice low-key one for upper primary writers. $100 prize plus the winning story published on the Book Links website. Open theme.

competitions.name: Territory Young Scientists Awards
competitions.pitch: NT kids build a bug out of pre-used materials and explain where it lives, or make a Crocwise poster. Teachers enter. Prizes given in Darwin in November.
competitions.when: Entries through Term 2 and Term 3, closing the Friday of the last week of Term 3

competitions.name: ACMF National Songwriting Competition
competitions.pitch: Nearly $20,000 in prizes, all paid towards musical equipment or tuition. A breakthrough comp for any kid who writes songs in their bedroom.

competitions.name: Tasmanian Science Talent Search
competitions.pitch: Tasmanian kids from Kinder to Year 12 decode the universe with a picture book, photo essay, video or invention. Kinder to Year 2 gets its own division.
competitions.cost_raw: Paid - $10 per entry for STAT members, $25 for non-members

competitions.name: Nunga Kids Art Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by SA's Commissioner for Aboriginal Children and Young People. First Nations kids' art on the Children's Day theme is displayed during NAIDOC Week.

competitions.name: Poetry In Action Poetry Competition
competitions.pitch: One original poem, any Australian school kid. Winner takes $1,000 and their poem joins performances seen by over 100,000 students. Poet keeps copyright.

competitions.name: ArtStart at the Queen Victoria Museum and Art Gallery
competitions.pitch: For 25 years, teachers across Northern Tasmania have sent in student art. Selected pieces are hung, professionally presented, in a real museum gallery.
competitions.when: Entries close late October, exhibition opens mid December

competitions.name: Save The Frogs! Art Contest
competitions.pitch: Frog conservation through art. Open to all ages and free to enter, so Aussie kids are welcome. Quirky, niche and surprisingly popular.

competitions.name: National Schools Poster Competition (NSPC)
competitions.pitch: Kids design and run their own investigation, then share what they found on a digital poster. Cash prizes per division, plus a sustainability stream.

competitions.name: Flickerfest FlickerUp (Australian National Youth Competition)
competitions.pitch: The youth arm of Flickerfest, Australia's Academy Award qualifying short film festival. Winning films screen at Bondi beside the international lineup.
competitions.when: FlickerUp entries close 23 November, festival January 2027 at Bondi

competitions.name: Children's Week National Poster Competition
competitions.status: Confirmed, entries open for the 2027 poster
competitions.pitch: The winning drawing becomes the real national Children's Week poster, printed and sent to schools, libraries and councils around the country.

competitions.name: International Festival of Owls Kids' Art Contest
competitions.pitch: A small US festival comp that now draws entries from dozens of countries. A perfect home for kids who love owls. Original art only, posted to Minnesota.

competitions.name: Australian Cartoonists Association Prize (in theINmag)
competitions.pitch: Going since 1924. The ACA picks a winner from the cartoons kids send in to theINmag each issue. The winner gets a year of Inkspot, their own magazine.

competitions.name: Camp Australia Big Art Comp
competitions.pitch: Camp Australia runs a national art comp every term. Past prizes include hoodies printed with kids' own art and a trophy designed by The Brickman himself.

competitions.name: Crayola Creative Acts of Color (Open Call)
competitions.pitch: Crayola's year-round open call. Less about winning, more about joining a global creative movement. Kids share what they make, tagged #StayCreative.

competitions.name: State Premier's Reading Challenges
competitions.pitch: Not a competition, a challenge. Read books from your state's list and earn a certificate signed by the Premier. A big motivator for reluctant readers.
competitions.where: NSW, QLD, VIC, WA, SA, TAS

competitions.name: theINmag - publishing real creative kids
competitions.pitch: Your drawing, story or comic on a real printed page, in the hands of thousands of kids across Australia. Send in anything you've made, any time. Send it IN.

competitions.name: Sydney Royal Easter Show - Junior Arts & Crafts
competitions.pitch: Australia's biggest creativity showcase, running since 1869. Hundreds of junior classes, and winning entries hang in the Arts & Crafts Pavilion.

competitions.name: APSMO Maths Olympiad (Years 5-6)
competitions.pitch: For kids who light up at hard maths problems. Four contests, five questions each, no calculator. More about how creatively you got there than the answer.

competitions.name: Children's Rights Queensland Art Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by Children's Rights Queensland with the Queensland Family and Child Commission. Age-group winners shared over $2,000 in prizes in 2025.

competitions.name: Class Clowns
competitions.status: Confirmed by the organiser 2026-09-08, 2027 registrations open late October 2026
competitions.pitch: Run by the Melbourne International Comedy Festival. A free workshop with a pro comedian, then a real heat in front of a live audience. Top prize $1,500.
competitions.when: 2027 registrations open late October 2026, heats Term 1, National Grand Final at Melbourne Comedy Festival

competitions.name: Eckersley's Kids Colouring Competition
competitions.pitch: Grab a free colouring sheet at any Eckersley's store or online, colour it in however you like, and winners take home $50 Eckersley's gift cards.
competitions.when: Multiple times per year (Easter, holidays, Christmas)

competitions.name: Faber-Castell Create Your Mark
competitions.pitch: Faber-Castell and Cool Australia set a classroom brief each year. The school behind the most inspiring entries scores $1,500 of Faber-Castell products.

competitions.name: FIRST LEGO League (Australia)
competitions.pitch: Where kids fall in love with engineering. Teams build a LEGO robot to solve missions, then compete from regional level all the way to international.

competitions.name: Micador Brand Giveaways
competitions.pitch: Aussie-owned art supplies brand Micador runs regular giveaways like Win a Year of Micador, with ranges for toddlers right through to tweens.
competitions.when: No giveaway running that we can confirm

competitions.name: NSW Children's Week Art Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by the NSW Advocate for Children and Young People, with themes built around children's rights. Group entries are welcome, three age categories.

competitions.name: Oz Schools Instrumental Championships (OSIC)
competitions.pitch: State championships leading to a National Final for young piano, strings, drums and guitar players. Top placers play State Finals at iconic venues.

competitions.name: Smiggle Christmas Card Competition
competitions.pitch: Kids draw a Christmas card front cover and the winning design is printed on actual Smiggle Christmas cards. Prizes usually include vouchers and Smiggle gear.

competitions.name: Staedtler Secondary School Artist of the Year
competitions.pitch: Staedtler's annual high school comp with a $5,000 prize pool, judged by three professional Australian artists. Weekly draws give away $200 art packs.

competitions.name: Staedtler World Kids Colouring Day
competitions.pitch: Kids send in a drawing on the year's theme, and for every picture Staedtler donates to a Plan International project supporting girls' education.

competitions.name: Very Short Film Festival - Junior Category (VSFF)
competitions.pitch: Australia's coolest under-the-radar youth film festival. Selected films premiere in Hobart, then tour nationally. Phone footage is fine.

competitions.name: Wakakirri National Story-Dance Festival
competitions.pitch: Entered as a school. Over 10,000 students a year tell a story through dance, drama and music in professional theatres. Storytelling beats technique.

competitions.name: Just Write - For Kids (SA Public Libraries)
competitions.pitch: Run by Marion City Council's library network. First prize up to $200, second up to $100. Word limits 300-750 (9-10s) or 500-1,000 (11-13s). Open theme.

competitions.name: Young Archie
competitions.pitch: The little sibling of the Archibald. Kids paint or draw a portrait of someone who matters to them, and finalists hang in the Art Gallery of NSW.

competitions.name: Think Science! Competition (ANSTO)
competitions.pitch: Run by ANSTO, Australia's nuclear science organisation. Free to enter, with generous prizes for winning schools. Particularly strong at primary level.

competitions.name: Cossack Children's Art Awards
competitions.pitch: A regional WA gem. Kids get a 30x30cm canvas to paint, and finalists hang alongside the famous Cossack Art Awards. The overall winner takes home $300.

competitions.name: Dorothea Mackellar Poetry Awards
competitions.pitch: One of Australia's longest-running kids' poetry comps, named for the writer of My Country. Cash prizes, plus an annual anthology of the best poems.

competitions.name: Furphy Junior and Youth Literary Award
competitions.pitch: Goulburn Valley kids write a short story or a poem on any subject. First prize in each category is $300, judging is blind, and the author keeps copyright.

competitions.name: NSW Premier's Spelling Bee
competitions.pitch: The classic spoken spelling bee for NSW Years 3 to 6. Kids progress from class to school to regionals, with State Finals held at Penrith.
competitions.when: Enrolment 2 March to 5 June, State Final 6 November

competitions.name: NSW WriteOn Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by the NSW Department of Education with the State Library. Winning stories are published in the Best of WriteOn anthology, kids' words in print.

competitions.name: Spencil Art Prize
competitions.pitch: Run by Aussie stationery brand Spencil. Major prize packs worth $400 each are stuffed with art supplies, so the prize is fuel for the next masterpiece.

competitions.name: The Golden Pen (Scribblers Festival)
competitions.pitch: Run by Perth's kids' lit festival, Scribblers. The overall winner takes home an e-reader and book pack, and shortlisted writers get book subscriptions.

competitions.name: CYA Conference Hatchlings Award
competitions.pitch: Run by the CYA Conference for children's and young adult writers. Cash prizes of $100, $60 and $40, with categories across different writing forms.

competitions.name: Little Sydney Lives Photography Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by the City of Sydney. Kids capture the city through their own lens, phone snaps welcome, and selected photos exhibit outdoors in central Sydney.

competitions.name: Randolph Stow Young Writers Award
competitions.pitch: Cash prizes for prose and poetry from primary writers in WA's Midwest and Gascoyne. Winners get a perpetual trophy displayed at their school.

competitions.name: Shaun Tan Award for Young Artists
competitions.pitch: Named after picture book legend Shaun Tan. Winning art hangs for a month at Subiaco Library, professionally framed, with the City picking up the tab.

competitions.name: Whitsunday Voices Short Story Competition
competitions.pitch: Cash prizes for first, second and third in every age category, Grades 3 to 12. Any subject at all, with word limits that step up by year level.

competitions.name: Big Science Competition (ASI)
competitions.pitch: Run by Australian Science Innovations. Fifty minutes of problem solving in real-life contexts, and a pathway into their science extension programs.

competitions.name: Boroondara Literary Awards (Young Writers)
competitions.pitch: Run by Boroondara Library Service in Melbourne since 1999. The young writers categories share over $5,000 in prize money, huge for a council award.

competitions.name: Laura Literary Awards (Prose & Poetry)
competitions.pitch: A small-but-mighty comp from the Rocky River Writers Club in country SA, with prose and poetry streams. Note: entries must be posted, not emailed.

competitions.name: OM Kids Photo Competition (Australian National Maritime Museum)
competitions.pitch: Kids 16 and under photograph oceans and waterways, and three winners each take home an OM System Tough TG-7 underwater camera. It runs every year.

competitions.name: Reconciliation Day Poster Competition
competitions.pitch: ACT school kids draw an A4 poster on the year's Reconciliation Day theme. The winning school takes $1,000 and the poster can become a public mural.
competitions.when: Entries close 1 May, winner announced at the Reconciliation Day event in June

competitions.name: South Perth Young Writers Award (SPYWA)
competitions.pitch: Shortlisted writers score a one-on-one workshop with a published local author, and finalists are published in the SPYWA Anthology. Prizes up to $150.

competitions.name: Whitlam Institute What Matters? Writing Competition
competitions.pitch: The Whitlam Institute asks kids one question, what matters? Answer however you want. Top prize is $1,500 and every entry is read by a real human.

competitions.name: Banabae - We Are All Artists
competitions.pitch: Aussie kids' clothing brand Banabae prints the winner's art onto real clothes in their next collection. The winner also takes home a $500 voucher.

competitions.name: CBCA WA's Make Your Own Storybook Awards
competitions.pitch: Make a real book, cover to cover: original story, original illustrations, hand-bound, solo or in a duo. Run by the Children's Book Council of Australia (WA).

competitions.name: Crikey! Magazine Photography Competition (Australia Zoo)
competitions.pitch: Run by Australia Zoo and the Irwin family. Top prize is two nights at the Crocodile Hunter Lodge, worth over $1,800. Robert Irwin started out here.

competitions.name: Matific Maths Olympiad
competitions.pitch: A five-day online maths comp where participation comes first. Top schools win up to $1,500 and every student gets a certificate.
competitions.when: Registration 15 June to 9 August, competition 10 to 14 August

competitions.name: Operation Art
competitions.pitch: Entered through NSW schools. Fifty pieces of student art are gifted to The Children's Hospital at Westmead every single year.
competitions.when: Applications close late June for following year

competitions.name: Wild At Art
competitions.pitch: Run by the Australian Conservation Foundation. Kids make art about an Aussie threatened species, and judges look for heart over technical skill.

competitions.name: Australian Mathematics Competition (AMC)
competitions.pitch: Australia's oldest and biggest maths comp, entered through schools since 1978. Every student gets an award, and the Olympiad pathway starts here.
competitions.when: Registration closes 31 July, sat early August

competitions.name: Opti-MINDS Creative Sustainability Challenge
competitions.pitch: Prep to Year 6 kids get a division all their own. Queensland teams across 13 regions take seven weeks on a big challenge with zero outside help.
competitions.when: School registrations close mid June, challenges released mid July, team nominations close late July, regional events late August, state final October
competitions.cost_raw: Paid - $295 per school plus $55 per team

competitions.name: Prime Minister's Spelling Bee
competitions.pitch: A national spelling tradition for Years 3 to 8. Kids compete from school to a national final, and past winners have met the actual Prime Minister.
competitions.when: School round 20 July - 21 August; National Final September

competitions.name: Royal Adelaide Show - Junior Art, Craft & Design
competitions.pitch: Australia's largest junior art, craft and design display. Real prize money and real exhibition space in the Goyder Pavilion, from painting to pottery.
competitions.when: Entries close 17 July, Show in September

competitions.name: Tournament of Minds
competitions.pitch: Teams get six weeks on one big problem with zero adult help, then perform their solution to a live audience and face a surprise challenge on the day.
competitions.when: School registrations close around June, challenges released late June to July, team nominations close late July to mid August, tournaments in August, state finals September
competitions.where: National, run by a branch in every state and territory

competitions.name: Young ICT Explorers (YICTE)
competitions.pitch: Founded by SAP and free to enter, with about $30,000 in cash prizes each year. Kids build real tech projects, from coding apps to building robots.
competitions.when: Registration closes 1 July, projects close 31 July

competitions.name: Better Read Kids Writing Competition
competitions.pitch: Run by Sydney bookstore Better Read Than Dead. Every entry is published in an anthology, so just by entering, kids become published writers.

competitions.name: Young Territory Author Awards
competitions.pitch: NT kids write and make a real book, cover to cover. The Young Territory Author of the Year takes $500, and entries join a Darwin library collection.
competitions.when: Entries close 27 August, winners announced in Darwin in November

competitions.name: Celebrate Australia Primary School Art Competition
competitions.pitch: In its 20th year. Gladstone region primary kids make art about the Australia they care about, and chosen pieces travel to sister city Saiki in Japan.
competitions.when: Entries close late November, winners announced on Australia Day

competitions.name: Australian Geographic Nature Photographer of the Year - Junior Category
competitions.pitch: The comp Robert Irwin won as a kid. Run by the SA Museum with Australian Geographic. Junior winners take home $500 and every finalist gets exhibited.
